title: matrix-vector multiplication

atoms.evidence: as_strided_mv(mat, vec) — implements torch.matmul for the matrix-vector case from scratch
strideV = vec.stride() — explicit warning in 'Help - passing first test failing second' that the input may itself be non-contiguous, so must use original stride not assume 1
vec_expanded = vec.as_strided(mat.shape, (0, strideV[0])) — strided view to broadcast the vector
stride (0, strideV[0]) makes vec_expanded[i, j] = vec[j] — stride 0 in dim 0 = no-copy broadcast over rows; exercise text says 'use the second-last example... the one that involved a stride of zero'
(mat * vec_expanded).sum(dim=1) — but the broadcast is implemented manually via as_strided, not via PyTorch's automatic broadcasting, so this atom is conceptually incidental

notes: 5-atom strided exercise that is the canonical no-copy broadcast lesson. Note: the matmul-via-strides approach REPLACES PyTorch's broadcasting with explicit stride-0 — so listing broadcasting-rules feels false-positive-ish, but the conceptual atom (size-1/stride-0 = stretch) is the same skill. Marked incidental to capture this tension.
